title: Hidden Singularity and Fractal Dimensions for Extended Harper Operators
authors: Simon Becker, Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Igor Krasovsky
abstract: We prove that, for every irrational frequency, the spectra of the extended Harper family throughout the zero-measure regime have finite $1/2$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and lower box dimension at most $1/2$. Both numbers improve to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary. The proof is based on a family of unitary transformations, that specializes to the chiral transform of [BJK] for the case of the critical almost Mathieu. This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $α$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the fractal geometry of the energy spectrum for the extended Harper model, a model describing electrons in a magnetic field. Using spectral cover techniques derived from singular Jacobi operators, the authors prove that the spectrum has finite Hausdorff and box dimensions, establishing precise bounds that improve on specific critical boundaries. This work contributes to the understanding of spectral properties in quasi-periodic quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the fractal dimensions (Hausdorff, box-counting, packing) of the spectrum for the extended Harper model when the spectrum has zero measure.
main_result: The spectrum is shown to have a Hausdorff and box dimension bounded by $1/2$ in the zero-measure regime, improving to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary.
method: The analysis uses unitary transformations to map the extended Harper operator to a singular Jacobi operator, allowing the application of spectral cover constructions based on canonical approximants of the irrational frequency $\alpha$.
model_or_system: The system is the extended Harper model (EHM), describing an electron on a square lattice in a perpendicular magnetic field, governed by a specific quasi-periodic Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Hausdorff measure ($	ext{meas}_{1/2}$), Hausdorff dimension ($\dim_H$), and Box dimension ($\dim_B$) of the spectrum $\Sigma_{\alpha, \lambda}$.
important_parameters: Irrational frequency $\alpha$, coupling parameters $\lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3)$, and the regime parameters defining the zero-measure set ($C_0$) and the isotropic boundary ($B_{iso}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes $\alpha$ is irrational and relies on the existence of canonical approximants $p_n/q_n$ for $\alpha$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the spectral equivalence to a singular Jacobi operator, then constructing spectral covers using techniques related to canonical approximants, and finally applying dimension theory bounds to these covers to determine the fractal dimension of the spectrum.
why_interesting: The study of fractal spectra in quasi-periodic systems is central to understanding localization phenomena, which is a key topic in condensed matter physics, particularly in the context of disordered or quasi-periodic potentials.
